title: Routes, RPC and the dev server — Vyrn docs

chapter.title: Routes, RPC and the dev server
chapter.lede: `std/ui` turns a routes directory into one function from request to response. `std/rpc` makes a typed call between the two halves. `vyrn dev` serves both while you work.

sections.heading: Routes
prose: std/ui reads a routes/ directory and generates one route(req) -> Response. Each route gets a typed URL helper, so a link cannot name a page that is not there. A [param].vyx file binds a path segment, and the component decides whether the value is a page or a 404.
This site is built with it: site/export.vyrn calls that function once per path and writes what comes back. The same table can be served live with vyrn serve instead.

sections.heading: RPC
prose: std/rpc generates the client and server halves of a call from one declaration. The client half runs in the page as wasm; the server half is a route. An answer is typed too: a rejection carries its validation issues attached to the fields they are about, so a form can show each problem where it belongs.

sections.heading: vyrn dev
prose: vyrn dev builds the client to wasm and serves the server, the static files and the runtimes in one process. vyrn routes prints the resolved table: every path the router mounts, each with its source. Read it first when a URL does not do what you expected.
